subject: Biotechnology
title: Dual-Use Research of Concern
description: One-minute skill: Dual-Use Research of Concern.

hook.text: The same research that creates a vaccine can create a weapon — dual-use dilemmas haunt biotechnology.

buildup.text: Gain-of-function studies enhance pathogen transmissibility to study pandemics — but they also create pandemic-capable viruses.

discovery.text: In 2012 two labs made H5N1 airborne-transmissible in ferrets — sparking a global debate on publishing dangerous methods.

twist.text: A US moratorium paused gain-of-function funding from 2014 to 2017 — then research resumed under a new oversight framework.

climax.text: The NSABB reviews dual-use research before publication — balancing scientific openness with biosecurity concerns.

punchline.text: Knowledge that heals can also harm — dual-use oversight guards the boundary.

quiz.question: Why are gain-of-function studies considered dual-use research of concern?
options: They require two different laboratories to complete
The same experiments that reveal pandemic risks also create pathogens with enhanced dangerous capabilities
They use both animal and human cells in the same experiment
